summary: Gorinchem's walled centre is regulated mainly through paid parking run by the municipality: the Kweeklust and Kazerneplein garages, the outer car parks Paardenwater, Buiten de Waterpoort and Bagijnenwal, and, according to a September 2024 presentation, well over 2,000 street spaces. The municipal designation decision (December 2024) set paid hours for the lower town of 10:00-22:00 Monday to Saturday plus Sundays from 12:30, with the upper town paid until midnight every day. New rates applied from 1 January 2025 (street 3.22 euros and garages 1.93 euros per hour; D66 councillors described the rise as about 40 percent, from 2.30 and 1.38 euros, and put the extra revenue at about 1 million euros a year), and the council adopted a further small rise on 16 December 2025 for 2026: 3.32 euros per hour for streets inside the ramparts and 2.00 euros in the garages. In a council presentation of 19 September 2024 the municipality showed 2024 figures of about 2.61 million euros of revenue against 1.59 million of costs (not stated whether actuals or forecast). The 2021 parking programme document (version 1.3, March 2021) aimed at a maximum average street occupancy of 80 percent, a freeze on new first resident permits and more evening use of garages by residents, and reported that surveys then showed night-time street occupancy above 90 percent in the southern parts of the upper and lower town; most of its measures were studies and intentions, and no later programme was found. The P+R Stationsweg (127 spaces) next to the railway station is listed in the national open-data register with NS as operator (a static tariff record whose entries date from 2021) and is presented on the Q-Park website; in June 2025 individual councillors said the large Q-Park facility is usually not used and asked why the P+R is used so little, which are remarks, not measurements. A draft framework for the station area, discussed in committee in June 2025, proposed a very low parking norm for new homes and offices; its adoption was not confirmed. Extra EV charging bays were designated at four neighbourhood sites in April 2025. No published occupancy statistics for the centre garages were found, and the municipal website was unavailable (HTTP 503) when checked.

items.text: The municipal parking ordinance for Gorinchem (version in force from 25 December 2025, page read on 21 October 2026) carries a 2026 tariff table: 2.00 euros per hour (incl. VAT) in the Kweeklust and Kazerneplein garages, 3.32 euros per hour for other streets inside the ramparts, 4.16 euros per hour at Groenmarkt / Achter de Kerk, and 1.66 euros per hour on the outer car parks Paardenwater and Buiten de Waterpoort, with a stated maximum of 4.98 euros (the table does not say for what period).
items.source_title: Parkeerverordening gemeente Gorinchem 2021 (current version, tariff table 2026)

items.text: Under the same ordinance (read 21 October 2026) the municipality issues residents', business, visitor, temporary-works and all-areas permits for at most one year. The first resident permit costs 98.60 euros per year, a second one 505.70 euros per year, and a business permit for one plate 629.55 euros per year; the visitor scheme costs 0.61 euros per hour.
items.source_title: Parkeerverordening gemeente Gorinchem 2021 (current version, tariff table 2026)

items.text: On 10 December 2024 the executive board designated the paid-parking areas and times (published 2 January 2025): in the lower town (Benedenstad) paid parking runs 10:00-22:00 Monday to Saturday and, newly, 12:30-17:00 on Sundays; the upper town (Bovenstad) runs 10:00-24:00 every day; the garages 10:00-17:00 (Thursday until 20:00) and Sunday 12:30-17:00. Public holidays New Year's Day and both Christmas days are free; this 2025 notice may since have been revised.

A written council question from D66 (24 December 2024) described the tariff rise from 1 January 2025 as a regular 10 percent index plus an extra 30 percent, taking street parking from 2.30 to 3.22 euros and garages from 1.38 to 1.93 euros per hour. It cited extra revenue of about 1 million euros a year, a letter of concern from the city-centre traders' association Hartje Gorkum, and asked the executive to explore a park-and-ride on the edge of town.
items.source_title: Schriftelijke vragen D66: Parkeren in de binnenstad wordt fors duurder

items.text: At a council theme session on 19 September 2024 the municipality presented 2024 parking figures (the slide does not say whether actuals or a forecast, and the year was not yet over): revenue of about 2.61 million euros (2.20 million from machines in streets and garages, 0.31 million permits, 0.10 million fines) against about 1.59 million euros of costs, a balance of about 1.02 million euros. It spoke of well over 2,000 street spaces in the centre and said that parking behind a barrier in municipal garages is an economic activity for which the municipality is VAT-liable.
items.source_title: Themasessie kosten en opbrengsten parkeren binnenstad (presentation, 19 September 2024)

items.text: The same presentation compared private parking in Gorinchem: Q-Park at the NS station charged 1.53 euros per hour (travellers 2.50 euros per day), the events hall 10 euros per parking action (varies per event) and Van der Valk 35 euros per parking action (guests free; a 'carpool tariff'). It also compared 2024 garage tariffs with Tiel (1.80 euros per hour), Gouda (2.00) and Dordrecht (1.50-2.75) against 1.38 euros in Gorinchem, and showed a proposal of 1.93 euros for Gorinchem garages.
items.source_title: Themasessie kosten en opbrengsten parkeren binnenstad (presentation, 19 September 2024)

items.text: On 15 April 2025 the municipality published a traffic decision (dated 8 April 2025) designating extra EV charging bays next to existing charge points at four neighbourhood sites (Kruithoorn in Hoog Dalem, Anna Blamanstraat in Laag Dalem, Arkelse Onderweg and Van Hoornestraat in Lingewijk), citing the National Agenda Charging Infrastructure.
items.source_title: Gemeenteblad 2025, 161789: aanwijzen parkeerplaatsen voor het opladen van elektrische voertuigen

items.text: The city's Parkeerprogramma binnenstad 2021-2025 (document of 30 March 2021, under the Mobiliteitsvisie 2040) aimed for at most 80 percent average occupancy of centre street spaces, keeping paid parking as the regulation tool, and freezing new first resident permits; it recorded night-time street occupancy above 90 percent, locally over 100 percent, in the southern parts of the upper and lower town. It is an older plan; later programme versions were not found.

The same 2021 programme counted 830 resident permits in the upper town (832 street spaces) and 959 in the lower town (674 street spaces, plus access to the two garages, 1,382 spaces in total), and noted that the outer car park Bagijnenwal was structurally above 80 percent occupied in the evening while Paardenwater had room.

According to the 2021 programme the centre has two barrier garages (Kweeklust and Kazerneplein, pay on exit) and three outer car parks without barriers (Buiten de Waterpoort, Bagijnenwal, Paardenwater, pay in advance). Its measures were mostly studies and intentions: a project to assess expanding Kweeklust (no concrete follow-up steps yet), research into expanding Bagijnenwal, an investigation of whether Kazerneplein could be used by residents, a research track on the parking guidance system, starting garage occupancy monitoring, and digitalising permits.

The 2021 programme said research showed a need for 95 public charging posts in Gorinchem, with the number in the historic centre capped per quadrant (for appearance and because of the high parking pressure), and that the feasibility of a car-sharing pilot in part of the centre was being investigated (shared cars were then offered by Visscher2Go).

The national parking open-data register (NPR, read 21 October 2026) lists the P+R Stationsweg at Stationsweg 21 with 127 spaces, no charge points, open 24/7, operator given as Nederlandse Spoorwegen, with a static tariff record of 1.46 euros per hour and 6.69 euros per day; the tariff entries in the record carry start dates of June 2021, so the tariff may be out of date.
items.source_title: RDW NPR open data: P+R Stationsweg (Gorinchem), static record

items.text: In the council committee session of 26 June 2025 on the station-area framework, one councillor asked what would happen to the large Q-Park facility at the station that 'is usually not used', and another suggested investigating why so little use is made of the P+R options; these are councillors' remarks, not measurements.
items.source_title: Parallelsessie Beraad & Advies, Uitgangspunten Stationsgebied, 26 juni 2025 (summary report)

items.text: In the committee session of 26 June 2025 councillors discussed the draft framework (Uitgangspunten Stationsgebied) for redeveloping the station area as part of the 'Vleugels van de stad' transformation. According to the discussion the paper proposed the lowest possible parking norm for homes and offices and looked at double use of parking for the city centre; the VVD group wanted active talks with Q-Park and NS so that the P+R function stays in balance, and a Gorcum Actief councillor said that the redesign of Banneweg, the roundabout and Touwbaan would remove parking places. The proposal went on to the council meeting of 10 July 2025; its adoption was not confirmed.
items.source_title: Parallelsessie Beraad & Advies, Uitgangspunten Stationsgebied, 26 juni 2025 (summary report)

items.text: The council adopted the 4th amendment of the Parkeerverordening on 16 December 2025 (published 24 December 2025), with the 2026 tariff table applying from 1 January 2026 and the supplementary assessment (fine) for non-payment raised from 78.80 to 82.00 euros. Compared with the 2025 designation decision, the garage rate rose from 1.93 to 2.00 euros and street parking from 3.22 to 3.32 euros per hour.

In December 2025 (published 1 December 2025) the municipality published a policy on exemptions for the access-restricted city centre: a pedestrian zone (Groenmarkt, Grote Markt, Hoogstraat and 12 other streets), a pedestrian area at Buiten de Waterpoort and a low-traffic street (Westwagenstraat). Exemptions are granted for immediate loading and unloading of goods, for fetching or bringing people who can reasonably only be fetched or brought by vehicle, for reaching an own or rented parking space on private land, and for works at an address, as day, temporary (2 days to 6 months) or annual passes issued per licence plate.

Q-Park's website (read 21 October 2026) lists P+R Stationsweg, Stationsweg, 4205 AA Gorinchem, with 127 spaces, open 24/7 with licence-plate recognition, bicycle parking and disabled bays, and a traveller discount for a domestic train trip returning the same day; the tariff block did not load on the page.

In November 2025 (published 11 November 2025) the municipality published a traffic decision for the reconstruction of Banneweg and Stationsweg between the Beatrix hospital and the station square: new cycle paths, a bus lane on Stationsweg, a new Banneweg-Mollenburgseweg roundabout, and removal of the Stadhuisplein car park connection to roundabout De Kom (access moved to a new entry and exit on Banneweg). The decision mentions adjacent car parks and designates a few disabled and EV bays there but gives no total space counts.
items.source_title: Gemeenteblad 2025, 485418: Diverse verkeersmaatregelen Banneweg, Mollenburgseweg en Stationsweg

gaps: https://www.gorinchem.nl/parkeren and other gorinchem.nl pages returned HTTP 503 on 21 October 2026, so the municipal parking pages (garage capacities, subscriptions, permit rules, P+R information) could not be read.
https://www.mooigorinchem.nl (Kweeklust garage page) was offline (maintenance notice) when fetched.

Garage capacities (Kazerneplein, Kweeklust), garage operator details beyond the municipal-run statement and the current garage tariffs on the street were only found on listing portals (centrumparkeren.nl), which are not used as support.
No 2026 designation decision (paid-parking hours and areas) was found; the hours in the items come from the December 2024 decision (Gemeenteblad 2025, 2052), which may have been revised.

Council papers for the 2026 tariff decision (raadsvoorstel Dec 2025) and any evaluation of the 2025 tariff rise, answers to the D66 questions, the outcome of the Kweeklust garage expansion, the parking guidance system and any new parking programme after 2025 could not be found: the iBabs council portal lists are loaded dynamically and no further web searches were possible (search budget exhausted).

No occupancy or utilisation statistics for the centre garages or the P+R were found in official documents; the only statements are councillors' remarks (June 2025) and the 2021 programme's occupancy findings.

EV charging: only the April 2025 traffic decision for four neighbourhood sites was found; no figures on charge points in the garages or the centre, and the NPR record lists no charge points at the P+R.
The Q-Park P+R Stationsweg page did not load its tariff block, and no official NS or Q-Park tariff for 2026 could be confirmed; the NPR tariff is a December 2024 static record.
Station-area redevelopment: the council decision adopting the framework (after the 26 June 2025 committee session) and any plan for the P+R site were not found.
Low-emission or environmental zones: no source found (none appears to exist in Gorinchem; not confirmed).
Local press (AD/Gorcums nieuws) was not searched or read.
